Parasitoids of whiteflies and scales; some hyperparasitoids
Unknown biology but likely egg parasitoids of Perloridiidae (Huber et al. 2025); definitely associated with mosses.

Parasitoids of whiteflies.
Many Dirhininae are saprophage-parasitoids in temporary habitats (parasitoids of fly larvae in carrion, dung etc). This is likely to be the dominant life history in the clade.
Associates of insect galls on trees, as inquilines or parasitoids. The latter is assumed here to be the dominant life history.
Life history unknown.
The Cleonyminae are associated with hosts in wood. The Ditropinotellinae are possibly phytophagous. Most of the remaining species are likely to be parasitoids of phytophagous hosts on plants.

Ormyridae and Cynipencyrtidae are phytophage-parasitoids, specifically parasitoids of gallers, and this is the likely ancestral trait. Most of the remaining species are likely phytophagous (gallers or inquilines) but some are parasitoids. It is assumed here that the majority of the species in the clade are phytophagous in MG. In SE, however, the fauna is limited to parasitoids.
Ooderini associated with hosts in wood.

Some Megastigmus are phytophagous. The life history of Keiraninae is unknown. Jansta et al. (2018) show parasitoids are basal. It is assumed here that the dominant life history in the group is to be parasitoids of phytophagous insects..
Potentially same parasitoid hosts as Asaphesinae (same clade), but biology unknown.
The Louriciinae may be associated with hosts in wood.
Almost certainly parasitoids of large wood-boring beetles, potentially including Cerambycidae (Gupta et al., 2022).
The life history of Cicedellis unknown.

The Akapalinae are possibly phytophage-parasitoids. The Eucharitidae are ant parasitoids, so would be classified here as saprophage-parasitoids in temporary habitats (see coding of ants). Some taxa, such as Monacon and Steffanolampus are associated with hosts in wood. However, the dominant life history in the clade is assumed to be phytophage-parasitoids of hosts in or on plants.
The Sycophaginae and Otitesellinae are phytophagous.
Life history unknown
